## PG&E Warns Customers to "Skip the Kiosk" to Avoid Utility Scams


November 17, 2026


*During 2026, PG&E customers have lost over $300,000 to scammers*


OAKLAND, Calif.


, Nov. 17, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- With the holidays upon us, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) urges customers not to allow utility scammers to take advantage of the hustle and bustle of the holiday season to steal


your money through deceptive, high-pressure tactics. This Wednesday, November 18 is Utility Scam Awareness Day to drive awareness of the signs of a scam so that customers can avoid falling victim.


Reports of scams targeting PG&E customers have remained alarmingly high throughout 2026. In fact, there have been over 10,000 reports year-to-date with customer losses exceeding $300,000, and an average loss of $929.


And, while scammers continuously adopt new methods to defraud utility customers, one common tactic is that they will demand that you make payment using a specific method, such as visiting a payment kiosk at a store, or by pre-paid debit cards or money transfer services to avoid immediate disconnection of your utility services.


"Remember, PG&E will never demand that you make payment via a specific method, such as visiting a payment kiosk at a retail store, by a scannable bar code or QR code, or by pre-paid debit card or online money transfer services. If someone on the phone or at your door is threatening to disconnect your utility services if you don't make immediate payment, hang up, close the door and end the scam. Then, you can visit[PGE.com/waystopay](http://pge.com/waystopay) to check your balance and to view options for bill payment," said Matt Foley, PG&E Protective Intelligence Analyst.


Small and medium-sized businesses are also a target, and scammers will focus their efforts during busy business hours, preying on business owners' sense of urgency to keep the doors open and the lights on. In fact, PG&E has received nearly 1,000 reports of scam attempts targeting these customers during 2025.


**Tips to Stay Safe and Avoid Falling Victim:**


- If you receive a call threatening disconnection if immediate payment is not made, hang up and end the call. Remember, PG&E will NEVER call and request any payment information over the phone, and we will never ask you to make payment via a specific method like a payment kiosk, pre-paid debit cards or through online money transfer services.
- Log into "My Account" at[PGE.com](http://pge.com/) to check your account status or call PG&E customer service at 1-800-743-5000. NEVER use a phone number provided by the suspected scammer.
- Report the incident immediately to PG&E by calling 1-833-500-SCAM or by visiting[PGE.com/scams](http://pge.com/scams) and by calling local law enforcement. Reporting is key, as PG&E works with law enforcement agencies to spot trends in scam attempts and to educate customers on how to spot scams and avoid falling victim.


**How customers can protect themselves**


- **Signing up for an online account at[pge.com](http://pge.com/) is an important safeguard** . Not only can customers log in to check their balance and payment history, they can sign up for recurring payments, paperless billing and helpful alerts.
- **Scammers Impersonating Trusted Phone Numbers:** Scammers are now able to create authentic-looking 800 numbers which appear on your phone display. If called back, the numbers do not lead back to PG&E. If a customer has doubts about the authenticity of the call, they should hang up and call PG&E at 1-833-500-SCAM. If customers ever feel that they are in physical danger, they should call 911.
- Customers who suspect that they have been victims of fraud


, or who feel threatened during contact with a scammer, should contact local law enforcement. The Federal Trade Commission's website is also a good source of information about how to protect personal information.


For more information about scams, visit[pge.com/scams](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4825196-1&h=2686288803&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com%2Fen_US%2Fresidential%2Fcustomer-service%2Fhelp%2Fscams%2Fscams.page&a=pge.com%2Fscams) or[consumer.ftc.org](http://consumer.ftc.org/) .


**About PG&E**


Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of[PG&E Corporation](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4825196-1&h=3476750293&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge-corp.com%2F&a=PG%26E+Corporation) (NYSE:PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit[www.pge.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4825196-1&h=310011630&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com&a=www.pge.com) and[http://www.pge.com/about/newsroom/](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4825196-1&h=2440162885&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com%2Fabout%2Fnewsroom%2F&a=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com%2Fabout%2Fnewsroom%2F) .
